thread:
Kai: short note: i've been chewing on correctness when we eagerly evict tombstones from prefix cache. proposal: instead of keeping the full tombstone we keep a tiny opaque 'stale-marker' per prefix for a short window. demote can consult this marker to decide whether to fetch from remote rather than serve a possibly-stale local value. initial reactions? :thinking:

Maya: interesting. what exact guarantee are we trying to preserve? per-tenant read-after-write, or stronger cross-shard causal visibility?

Kai: aim is pragmatic: guarantee read-after-write within a single logical prefix/tenant. we currently demote->remote when prefix missing; if we drop tombstone entirely a concurrent writer could be invisible to a reader until remote sync, causing surprising stale reads. marker detects recent commits cheaply.

Dani: tradeoffs: marker size, metadata churn, and TTL. if we keep marker too long metadata grows; too short and it doesn't protect against races. my pick: 8 bytes (5-byte commit-epoch + 3-byte checksum), TTL configurable per deployment.

Sam: where is marker stored? we must avoid causing extra slab moves. putting it in a separate object may blow up compaction. embedding in prefix header seems better but is header hot on updates?

Kai: agree — embed in prefix header. header updates are smaller and already handled by our slab write path. we only update marker on commit so write amplification is limited.

Maya: race scenario: reader demote reads marker, sees it's old, decides to SERVE_LOCAL; but a writer commits immediately after demote decision and before remote fetch — reader could still get stale response. does that break our intended guarantee?

Dani: depends on when marker is written in commit path. If commit path updates marker synchronously before acknowledging writer, the reader will see it if it arrives after writer ack. We need to formalize: guarantee = "if writer received successful ack before reader request, reader must not see pre-write state." Achieve by updating marker atomically during commit.

Sam: here's a slimmed API for the demote decision:

DemoteResult demote(prefix, req_epoch) {
  marker = read_marker(prefix) // epoch or 0
  if (marker >= req_epoch) return FETCH_REMOTE
  else return SERVE_LOCAL
}

Kai: req_epoch is derived from read timestamp (or 0 if caller doesn't care). marker is last-committed epoch. If marker >= req_epoch we force a fetch to ensure up-to-date state.

Maya: test plan: we need deterministic race tests that can interpose eviction and force the three critical windows: writer-before-evict, writer-during-evict, writer-after-evict (with slow remote apply). This should cover most surprising cases.

Dani: telemetry: demote_invocations, demote_forced_fetches, demote_false_negatives (served local but remote had newer data), marker_memory_bytes. With these we can tune TTL for real workloads.

Sam: compaction consideration: backend GC that removes tombstones should also remove markers; otherwise markers could pin metadata forever. compaction must clear marker atomically when it clears tombstone.

Kai: lifecycle sketch: on commit -> write marker(epoch) synchronously; eviction may evict value but retain marker until TTL or compaction; compaction clearing tombstone clears marker. For prefix handoff/migration, copy marker and adjust TTL offset so new shard honors remaining protection window.

Maya: privacy note: markers must be opaque and not include any key material. store only epoch+crc or another non-sensitive digest.

Dani: corner cases: cross-shard migrations, multi-prefix transactions, and rollback scenarios. For multi-prefix txn we need to update markers for all touched prefixes in the same commit path.

evict-bot: RFC stub linked: https://redwood.internal/rfc/kv-prefix-marker (auto: watchers eng-runtime, eng-platform)

Sam: next steps: draft RFC follow-up with storage encoding (8 bytes), header layout, compaction integration, and canary plan (dev cluster, 2-week soak, metrics). include API pseudocode and a flag to toggle sync vs async marker updates for perf experiments.

Kai: decisions to make in RFC: marker size (8 vs 16), default TTL (30s vs 5m), sync-on-commit vs async (we lean sync for correctness), plus instrumentation points.

Maya: +1 for sync-on-commit initially. we can flip to async behind a feature flag if perf shows write amplification.

Dani: i'll author the race-test harness and metrics dashboard queries. will add alert thresholds for demote_false_negatives.

Kai: thanks. will draft the RFC and include a debug trace flag to surface marker state in tenant traces to help oncall. please add gotchas to the PR.

Sam: :thumbsup:
